title: Pisot units and the third manuscript on page 343 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook, with a verification script and calculator
description: Andrews and Berndt (Ramanujan's Lost Notebook, Part IV, Sect. 7.4) could not give a meaning to Ramanujan's claims on page 343 and wrote that they are wrong. We show that a = 1/(2^(1/5)-1) = 1+θ+θ^2+θ^3+θ^4 and b = √5/(1+4^(1/5))^(5/2) = 1-θ-θ^2+θ^4 (θ = 2^(1/5)) are units of Z[θ], that each factor of Ramanujan's error term is the modulus of a Galois conjugate of a^m b^n, and that the integer is Tr(a^m b^n θ). This proves (7.4.1) with the bound 2θ(|σ1(a^m b^n)|+|σ2(a^m b^n)|); the constant 2θ is sharp and the bound tends to 0 exactly along sequences with m − 6.0114 n → ∞. The number 1/(2^(1/p)−1) is a Pisot number if and only if p ≤ 6, which explains why the case 2^(1/7) in (7.4.2) needs further units; the printed (7.4.2) differs from the conjugate moduli in three places and its corrected form holds on an explicit cone. The record contains a 6-page note, a Python script with 15 checks (SymPy, mpmath), an offline calculator, the figure code and two OEIS drafts.
